title.value: Amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies for people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease
title.quote: Amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies for people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease

design.quote: This Cochrane review was funded in part by

n.quote: Overall, we included 17 studies with 20,342 participants.

population.value: people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease
population.quote: people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease

intervention.value: amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies aducanumab, bapineuzumab, crenezumab, donanemab, gantenerumab, lecanemab, ponezumab, remternetug, and solanezumab
intervention.quote: amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies aducanumab, bapineuzumab, crenezumab, donanemab, gantenerumab, lecanemab, ponezumab, remternetug, and solanezumab

phase.location: Criteria for considering studies for this review, Types of studies

outcomes.name: cognitive function as measured by the ADAS‐Cog (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale‐Cognitive) scale
outcomes.quote: Compared to placebo, amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies probably result in little to no difference in cognitive function as measured by the ADAS‐Cog (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale‐Cognitive) scale (standardised mean difference (SMD) −0.11, 95% confidence interval (CI) −0.16 to −0.06; 13 studies, 9895 participants; moderate certainty).
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Our outcomes of critical importance were: cognitive function

outcomes.name: dementia severity as measured by the CDR‐SB (Clincal Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes) scale
outcomes.quote: Amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies may result in little to no difference in dementia severity as measured by the CDR‐SB (Clincal Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes) scale (SMD −0.12, 95% CI −0.24 to −0.00; 9 studies, 8053 participants; low certainty).
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Our outcomes of critical importance were: cognitive function; dementia severity

outcomes.name: functional ability as measured on the ADCS‐ADL (Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study ‐ Activities of Daily Living) scale
outcomes.quote: Amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies probably result in little to no difference in functional ability as measured on the ADCS‐ADL (Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study ‐ Activities of Daily Living) scale (SMD 0.09, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.16; 3 studies, 3478 participants; moderate certainty)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Our outcomes of critical importance were: cognitive function; dementia severity; functional ability

primary_endpoint_status.quote: The effect of amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies on cognitive function and dementia severity at 18 months in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease is trivial, while on functional ability, it is small at best.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The review found that amyloid-beta-targeting monoclonal antibodies resulted in trivial or no clinically meaningful differences in cognitive function, dementia severity, and functional ability compared to placebo.

deaths.quote: overall mortality (ARD 2 more events per 1000, 95% CI 3 fewer to 11 more; 7 studies, 9733 participants; high certainty).

serious_adverse_events.quote: At 18 months, amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies do not increase serious adverse events (ARD 6 more events per 1000, 95% CI 10 fewer to 26 more; 9 studies, 11,904 participants; high certainty)

disagreements.question: reimbursement by the UK NHS
disagreements.position: benefits are too small to justify the cost to the NHS
disagreements.attributed_to: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
disagreements.quote: the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence expressed a negative opinion about its reimbursement by the UK NHS (National Health System) since benefits are too small to justify the cost to the NHS [].

disagreements.question: net clinical benefit for people with AD
disagreements.position: does not offer benefit to patients with MCI or early dementia due to AD
disagreements.attributed_to: German Institute for Quality and Efficiency in German Healthcare (IQWIG)
disagreements.quote: Recently, the German Institute for Quality and Efficiency in German Healthcare (IQWIG) concluded that lecanemab does not offer benefit to patients with MCI or early dementia due to AD [].

The publication of this article was supported by "Ricerca Corrente" funding from the Italian Ministry of Health.
limitations: The external validity of the study results for the wider AD population is limited.
We found notable heterogeneity amongst studies in the outcomes of efficacy and in the tools that the study authors used to assess them.
An important limitation of the available published literature is the lack of data on symptomatic ARIA
we had some concerns with respect to efficacy outcome measures, the magnitude of which may have been substantially impacted by functional unblinding.
All included studies were funded by the pharmaceutical industry
Another limitation of the evidence on amyloid‐beta‐targeting monoclonal antibodies is the lack of extractable data on the education level of participants

risk_of_bias.quote: for the efficacy outcomes, we judged the overall risk of bias as "some concerns" for all studies, due to bias in measurement of the outcomes, as adverse effects (i.e. infusion reaction) were much more frequent in the treated arm, which could lead to functional unblinding.
